title: Game 6: Chajes–Capablanca
subtitle: Active defence turns a dangerous position into a win

narration.say: Chajes has White against Capablanca in the Rice Memorial Tournament of 1916. Black chooses the McCutcheon Variation.
White advances e5. Black exchanges on c3 and centralises the knight.
White retreats the bishop. Black attacks the centre.
White brings the rook to d1. Both sides improve their pieces.
Capablanca presents the knight on d5 as a key restriction on White’s attack.
White lifts a rook toward the kingside. Black completes development and brings the queen to b4.

steps.title: A pawn capture opens the attack

narration.say: White captures en passant on f6. Black recaptures, and the h-pawn exchange opens more lines.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Sacrifice the rook on h6 with check.

steps.title: A knight check wins the queen

narration.say: White checks with the knight. The e-pawn captures it, opening the queen’s route to b4.
Black has given up the queen but keeps active pieces and attacking chances.
White invades with the rook. Capablanca criticises his defensive choices in this phase.
White exchanges a rook for the attacking rook on g6. The black king recaptures.
White centralises the queen and begins improving the bishop.
Black gives rook checks, but White keeps the queen active.
White opens lines with a pawn advance, then creates a dangerous passed pawn.

steps.title: Do not rush to collect material

narration.say: White keeps the attacking bishop active instead of immediately taking the pawn on g4.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Place the bishop on g7.

steps.title: Meet the advanced pawn with coordinated defence

narration.say: Black pushes toward promotion. White activates the king and queen.
White brings the queen to h3. A series of exchanges removes the passed pawn and Black’s rook.

steps.title: The queen and king finish the job

narration.say: White takes the remaining queenside pawn and brings the king forward.
Black resigns. The game ends at the final move recorded in the book.

steps.title: Activity matters after a material imbalance

narration.say: White’s combination won the queen, but Black’s active pieces made the position far from trivial.
Chajes coordinated queen, bishop and king, avoided unnecessary risk and dealt with the promotion threat.
Capablanca records several chances he missed. The lesson is to evaluate concrete activity, not just count material.
